dossier.public_summary: The dip looks different when it returns: about half as deep in sector 55 as in sector 82 for the same pipeline, and the three individual transits also disagree. There is also a strong secondary dip about one third the depth of the primary and an odd-even depth difference. That instability, together with a low planet score, matches a blended or binary eclipse or systematic variability better than a planet on the target.

reasons.why: depth changes by ~80% between sectors (6941 +/- 2451 ppm in sector 55 vs 16265 +/- 1441 ppm in sector 82) with chi2 10.76 dof 1, highly inconsistent for a planet on the target
variation persists within a single source (TESS-SPOC), with Chi-square confirming it is not a calibration offset
individual transit depths are also inconsistent (only 3 transits, share 0.4875), inconsistent with a stable planetary signal

significant secondary near 0.2969 phase with depth ~35% of primary and SNR close to brightening threshold, and odd_even diff_sigma 2.032 with depth ratio 1.5, together favour an eclipsing binary blended/variable rather than a planet
ML scorer ranks as planet-like as median planet only 10th percentile, consistent with binary/blend interpretation supported above
